title: Compact telemetry payload v2 - sketch
content:
Context and motivation:
- current telemetry payload (v1) is verbose: per-request spans include full header blobs, repeated route metadata, and token-level timing arrays. Host costs and S3 storage retention for long-term traces are ballooning.
- we need a compact, privacy-first payload that preserves the signal SRE/SDK/Runtime teams need for root-cause, cost attribution, and model-quality regressions while trimming size by ~6-10x for typical p95 traces.
- v2 should be drop-in for the ingest pipeline (Kafka -> preproc -> clickhouse), but allow a controlled rollout (SDK opt-in + sampling policy).

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- reduce median trace size by ~6x, p99 by ~3x (target numbers rough).
- preserve key correlators: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), route, model_variant, region, latency buckets, error codes, token_count, cost_estimate.
- support differential payloads: full (on demand / heavy sampling), compact (default), sketch-only (very low fidelity for massive sampling).
- privacy: no raw user prompt or PII in default compact payloads. Allow policy-controlled redaction or hashed fingerprints for dev workflows.
- incremental adoption: SDKs produce v1 & v2 concurrently for a rollout window; server-side ingestion should accept both and upgrade to v2 canonical internally.

Constraints and principles:
- All fields should be typed and semantically versioned. Use a single top-level "schema_version" string ("v2.0") and a compact feature bitmask for optional sections.
- Keep arrays short and bucket numeric events where possible (e.g., token-latency histogram instead of per-token times).
- Use deterministic, fast hashing for tenant ids and prompt fingerprints (e.g., xxhash64) with salt managed in KMS.
- Avoid nested deep objects; flat key names with dotted convention allowed (e.g., "model.variant").

Proposed top-level payload (flat map, JSON compact representation):
- schema_version: "v2.0"
- ts: ISO8601 or epoch_ms string for event time
- req_id: short uuid (base62)
- tenant_hash: hex (xxh64-salted)
- route: string (short route id)
- model.variant: compressed string id (e.g., "gptx-8q8:2025-09-12")
- region: short code (e.g., "us-west-2")
- outcome: enum [ok, partial, error, timeout]
- latency.ms: integer total latency in ms
- token.count: integer
- cost.microunits: integer (micro-cents) -- precomputed estimate on agent side
- error.code: optional short code (if outcome!=ok)
- sampling.tier: enum [full, default, sketch]
- features.mask: base64 bitmask of optional sections present (see mask map below)
- telemetry.flags: comma-list (e.g., "kvcache:miss,cachewarm:1")

Optional sections (included when features.mask indicates):
- hist.token_latency: small histogram encoded as list of buckets (e.g., "[0:120,1:30,2:10]") where bucket indexes are millisecond ranges mapped in static doc.
- prompt.fingerprint: hex (salted hash) -- no raw prompt unless full sampling
- trace.path: short list of endpoint hops (comma separated)
- model.metrics: comma-list key=value for small metrics (e.g., "ppl:12.3,mem_peak_mb:640")
- kvcache.hits: small counters (hit,miss,partial)
- structured.annotations: base64 CBOR of small assertion objects (used only in full sampling)

Encoding choices and rationale:
- JSON over wire but encourage gzipped newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for shipping. Consider LZ4 framing for extremely high-throughput lanes.
- Use compact names to save bytes (e.g., "t" for "ts" is okay but prefer clarity in v2 until v3).
- For histograms, use a compact run-length or bucket-key format to avoid long arrays.
- When possible, encode small repeated enums as single chars (mapping table agreed in infra).

Privacy controls and redaction modes:
- default (compact): no prompt text, only prompt.fingerprint if enabled by tenant policy.
- developer-debug (full): allowed for internal tenants and must be explicitly enabled via SDK knob + consent flag. Full mode includes prompt text (optionally truncated) and per-token timings.
- anonymize: for regulated tenants, we may drop tenant_hash and set tenant_anonymized=true; billing uses alternate aggregation lane.

Sampling strategy (runtime + SDK cooperative):
- Default: sample default tier at 2% for full payload, 20% for default compact payloads remain. Sketch tier: for 100% but extremely thin (minimal keys) for cost attribution.
- Adaptive sampling: increase full sampling for error rates above threshold, or for routes with sudden latency spikes.
- SDKs will emit "sampling.hint" header to the runtime to coordinate. Ingress preprocessor respects header but ultimately enforced by central sampler to control volume.

Transition plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (Q4 pilot): SDKs optionally emit v2 alongside v1 for a limited set of tenants (internal + canaries). Consumer infrastructure accepts both.
- Phase 1 (Q1 opt-in): broader SDK rollout with telemetry flags and opt-in docs. Pipeline tagging for v2 ingestion.
- Phase 2 (Q2 default): backend treats v2 as preferred; v1 still accepted but marked deprecated and logged.
- Phase 3 (TBD): hard cutover when downstream consumers updated (~6 months after Phase 2).

Example compact payload (NDJSON single line):
{"schema_version":"v2.0","ts":"2026-02-27T17:03:14Z","req_id":"x0plB3","tenant_hash":"3f94ab2c5e7f","route":"chat.v1","model.variant":"rwd-4-8q8:2026-01-11","region":"us-west-2","outcome":"ok","latency.ms":"112","token.count":"48","cost.microunits":"240","sampling.tier":"default","features.mask":"Cw==","telemetry.flags":"kvcache:miss"}

Open questions / risks (for discussion):
- feature bitmask scheme: use proto-like enum (simpler) vs base64 bitmask (more compact) — which wins for future extensibility?
- runtime mapping table: who owns the central enum->char map? infra or observability? Need governance doc.
- costs on the SDK: computing cost.microunits at client's side risks divergence with billing; should be treated as heuristic only.
- GDPR/CCPA: hashed tenant id is safer but still PD if salt leaks. KMS rotation policy needed.
- backward compatibility: some downstream analytic jobs expect token-level arrays. We'll need adapter jobs to synthesize histograms or a fallback ingestion path.

Action items (next steps):
- (Maya) draft a compact enum mapping doc and propose the initial character map for small enums. (Due: +1 week)
- (Arjun) prototype encoder/decoder in python and node; measure size reduction over 10k traces. (Due: +2 weeks)
- (Lena) open GH PR to add v2 opt-in to telemetry SDKs and a feature flag in Console for tenants to opt-in. (Due: +3 weeks)
- schedule sync with infra (kafka/preproc) and billing to agree on cost.microunits semantics.

Notes / stray ideas:
- consider using a stable binary format like CBOR for token-heavy full sampling mode; but keep compact lane JSON-friendly for log ingestion and human debugging.
- could add a short micro-schema for structured_annotations so downstream can index assertions (e.g., safety-fail,count).
- add a small (max 64B) free-form "s" slot for quick operational tags (e.g., "s:hotfix-314")

Quick links / references:
- slack convo: #observability -> thread "telemetry payload v2" (link pinned)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412 (proto encoder WIP)
- JIRA: OBSV-289 (v2 telemetry schema)

Status: this doc is a personal sketch, aiming to gather initial feedback from observability, runtime, and SDK leads. Will iterate toward a lightweight RFC after prototype numbers.

Notes-to-self: keep payload human-readable in default mode; we can always compress later. Mark any additional changes clearly in the schema_version so downstream can evolve without breaking.
